_method: Web search only. No venue was visited, phoned, or photographed. Every entry below was reached from a search-result page; see `source` on each one for what was actually read and `confidence` for what that does and does not establish.
_source_vs_lead: Per CLAUDE.md's data rules and the brief for this session: a venue's own Facebook page or its Google Maps listing is a SOURCE. A listicle, a travel blog, a review aggregator (Tripadvisor, Wanderlog, Trip.com, Evendo, kupi, petitfute, coool.cafe) or a taxi-company blog is a LEAD — it means someone says the place exists, not that anything about it is confirmed. Every entry records which it is.
_hours: Every `hours` below is null, and that is a finding rather than a gap. Facebook renders its page content behind a login/JS wall, so a fetch of a venue's own page returns the name and the city and nothing else — no address, no hours, no phone (verified on facebook.com/damdamcoffee, which returned exactly that). Google Maps listings are not fetchable the same way. Aggregator sites DO print hours, but an aggregator is a lead, and copying hours out of one is exactly the thing CLAUDE.md forbids. So: nobody should fill `hours` from this file. Hours come from opening the venue's own page, or from being there.
_popularity: There is no footfall or popularity data for Laos and none was used to order this list. Google's popular-times is not exposed in any Google API and is only available by scraping the Maps page, which is both against their terms and unreliable. There is no Lao equivalent of Yelp. The review counts on Tripadvisor/Wanderlog for Vientiane venues are in the low tens and are dominated by visitors rather than residents, so they measure tourist traffic, not whether a place is busy on a Tuesday. Anything that turns up claiming to be Lao footfall data should be treated as a lead and its provenance written down before it is used. Nothing in the app should be ordered by it.
_duplicates_checked: Cross-checked against all 30 ids in data/venues.json on 2026-09-13. Common Grounds, Tipsy Elephant, Wind West and Corebeer already exist and are excluded. `sinouk-pavilion-km9` is included deliberately: data/venues.json already has `sinouk-khemkhong`, but this is a different address (KM9 Thadeua Rd vs Quai Fa Ngum) and so is a different venue, not a duplicate — confirm before adding either way.

_batch_2: 2026-09-14, second unattended session. 24 RESTAURANTS appended to `candidates` below the 28 cafes/bars from 2026-09-13. Same rules, same file, nothing in the repo loads it. This batch was asked for restaurants specifically and for a district per venue; read _district_source for what `district` here does and does not mean, and _venue_type_blocker for why none of these can be entered yet even once verified.
_venue_type_blocker: NONE OF THESE CAN BE ENTERED AS-IS, and it is not a data problem. `restaurant` is not a venue type this app has. functions/api/_venue-validation.js line 15 is VENUE_TYPES = ['bar', 'cafe', 'venue'], so the API rejects it. js/app.js's COLORS map has no pin colour for it; pinSVG()'s glyphKey falls through to the generic 'venue' glyph; the Home filter matchType() only knows 'bar' and 'cafe'; index.html has no chip for it; css/style.css has no .marker.type-restaurant and :root has no --pin-restaurant; the owner form's Bar/Cafe .seg-btn toggle has two options. Entering these as type 'venue' would work and would be wrong - 'venue' is the ITECC/mall/night-market bucket. Adding the type is a real change across six files with two design decisions inside it (a pin colour that is not already spoken for, and a glyph), which is Kar's call rather than a side effect of a research pass. Do that first; this list cannot be used until then.
_district_source: `district`, `road_osm`, `village_osm` and `osm` come from the OpenStreetMap Nominatim search API, queried 2026-09-14. That is a third-party crowd-sourced record, NOT the venue's own statement - a strong lead for 'which district is this in', and nothing more. Rule applied: a result was accepted only when the returned display_name actually contains the venue's name. Nominatim fuzzy-matches and will confidently return a different business: it returned 'Lao Derm Som Nguem' 19km away for 'Lao Derm', and 'Mini Makphet' for 'Makphet'. Both were rejected, and both are written down so the query is not repeated and accepted. Where a venue has no `district` it is because OSM had no matching entry at all (6 of the 24) - coverage in Vientiane is patchy, and absence there says nothing about the venue. THE COORDINATES IN `osm` ARE NOT PINS. CLAUDE.md: a venue's lat/lng must be Kar-confirmed, and a pending venue carries NULL rather than a guess. They are here only so a place can be found on a map in order to check it; copying one into the venues table would put a stranger's guess on the map with pin_status 'placed'.

_closed_found.note: One venue was researched, found, and then found to be gone. Recorded rather than silently dropped, because it is the best single argument for the listicle rule.
_closed_found.evidence: Laotian Times, post dated 14 May 2025: 'Doi Ka Noi, a renowned restaurant in Vientiane Capital, has permanently closed after the death of its chef and owner, Ponpailin Noi Kaewduangdee, on 13 May.' https://www.facebook.com/laotiantimes/posts/doi-ka-noi-a-renowned-restaurant-in-vientiane-capital-has-permanently-closed-aft/1113098454177340/
_closed_found.why_it_matters: Doi Ka Noi was the first Lao restaurant to reach Asia's 50 Best (no. 86, 2025) and is still being recommended by travel listicles dated September 2026, sixteen months after it closed. A listicle is not a source. It is also the only positive closure signal found across 52 candidates in two batches, and it was found in a news post rather than on the venue's own page - consistent with _possibly_closed: the signals that would mark a venue closed sit on exactly the pages that cannot be read.

_name_lo_provenance: Every `name_lo` in this batch is COPIED from the Facebook page title as it appeared in the search result (or, for Kung's Cafe Lao, from the OpenStreetMap record), never transliterated or reconstructed. That distinction matters here more than usual: the unattended session writing this file cannot read Lao well enough to notice a wrong character, and a venue name with a typo in it is a venue nobody searching for it will find. A Lao speaker should still check each one against the live page before any of these become records - but the failure mode being guarded against is a name invented in transcription, and none of these were.
_facebook_wall: Re-tested 2026-09-14 on facebook.com/Kualao/. The result is unchanged from 2026-09-13: the fetch returns the business name in English and Lao, and 'Vientiane'. No address, no district, no phone, no hours, no permanently-closed marker. This is why every `hours` in this file is null and why `district` had to come from somewhere else entirely. It is not a gap that more searching closes.
_dedupe_within_file: The 2026-09-14 restaurant batch was cross-checked against the 30 ids in data/venues.json AND against the 28 entries already in this file, by source URL and by name. One hit: Kung's Cafe Lao, already present from the cafe batch on the same Facebook URL. The restaurant duplicate was removed and its OpenStreetMap district folded into the original entry, so this file has one row per venue. Nothing else in the restaurant batch matches either list - most of the restaurants sit in districts (Xaysetha, Sikhottabong) that the cafe/bar batch barely touched.
